findings: Minutes uses a separate native access DTO: window.minuteAccess. The client sets EncrItemID and sends the full DTO to POST /Services/api/GetMinutesAccess/?sct=... .
AccessStatus=1 is treated as locked. The client treats every other status as available; a safe adapter must establish an explicit allowed result rather than copy that fail-open branch.
Release uses POST /Services/api/RemoveMinutesAccess/?sct=... with the same access DTO. It is not the app2 item-lock release.
GetMinutes returns the minutes DTO directly. The client uses Minutes and IsEdit and preserves the remaining DTO for save.
SaveMinutes clones the whole DTO and encodes Minutes as base64(encodeURIComponent(html)). Its query repeats endid and includes enOVid for the explicit save variant.
